abstract:
China carries one of the heaviest burdens of hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection worldwide. This study aimed to estimate the prevalence of anti-HCV and incidence rate of HCV seroconversion in a large health check-up population in China.
This cross-sectional, and longitudinal study used data from the Meinian health check-up database, covering participants from all 31 provinces of mainland China between 2017 and 2023. Serological samples were tested for anti-HCV using ELISA. The weighted prevalence of anti-HCV and the incidence rate of HCV seroconversion were calculated. Poisson regression was used to identify risk factors for HCV seroconversion.
A total of 1,610,735 participants were included in the analysis of anti-HCV prevalence. The prevalence of anti-HCV in the study population was 0.89% (95% CI, 0.77%-1.01%), with significantly higher prevalence found in females and elderly individuals. Geographically, the prevalence was significantly higher in Central and West China compared to East China. Individuals with abnormal liver function or liver fibrosis, abnormal thyroid function or antibodies, diabetes, and impaired kidney function had significantly higher prevalence. The analysis of HCV seroconversion included 179,447 participants, showing an incidence rate of 0.72 per 1,000 person-years during a median follow-up of 1.5 years. Risk factors for HCV seroconversion included older age, as well as living in Central or West China, border regions, areas with low GDP per capita, and areas with high anti-HCV prevalence.
Our study reveals significant anti-HCV seroprevalence burden and ongoing risk of HCV transmission in a large health check-up population in China, highlighting the urgent need for systematic screening and enhanced prevention efforts to control HCV transmission.
